Design a cultural event poster with a modern Eastern editorial aesthetic. The core visual composition adopts the structure of "large color blocks + micro scene," incorporating subtle yet restrained paper collage and watercolor material language.

The composition uses large areas of low-saturation color blocks as the primary visual element, employing the [Main Color Palette] to establish a strong, cohesive large-scale spatial relationship. These color blocks can form abstract spaces such as mountains, riverbanks, courtyards, workshops, kites, or dyed fabrics through techniques like torn paper, layering, occlusion, enclosure, interweaving, suspension, diagonal extension, or negative space via white space—but avoid rendering them as ordinary realistic scenes. From afar, the composition first reveals a clear large color block layout, maintaining strong recognizability even in thumbnail view.

All color blocks should feature rich, authentic textures of handmade paper, watercolor pulp, and mineral pigments, visible with natural paper fibers, pigment sedimentation, subtle impressions, rubbings, natural gradations in tone, and irregular torn edges. The materials should be finely detailed and abundant yet keep a clean, intact quality—avoiding dirtiness, yellowing spots, severe damage, heavy granulation, or cheap vintage filters. The overall effect should present a matte, natural, breathable tactile sense of paper.

Between the expansive color blocks, incorporate a [micro scene] that is extremely small in scale but complete in content. Figures and props should occupy only about 2%–5% of the overall image, with the figures genuinely engaged in an activity rather than posing statically. Convey a small story through actions, objects, and spatial relationships—such as flying a kite, playing a qin, sipping tea, rubbings, sun-drying books, dyeing fabric, or pottery-making. The figures' clothing should be naturally restrained, unified with the overall cultural theme, without stealing the primary visual focus from the large color blocks.

The micro scene can include a small amount of [cultural elements], but control the quantity and information density. Props should be naturally scattered or integrated into the figures' actions, avoiding product display or overcrowding the frame. You can add a tiny warm-colored focal point, vermilion seal mark, lamplight, moon, or object hue as an accent, typically limited to 1%–3% of the image.

Typography should employ a restrained Eastern editorial design language. The main title [Title Text] uses elegant Chinese Song-style, Ming-style, or modern fonts with a publishing sensibility; keep the font size moderate, with ample white space, positioning the text as the secondary visual layer rather than overwhelming the image with massive typography. Supporting English text, dates, locations, and event details use even smaller font sizes to form a clear information hierarchy. All text must carry real meaning—do not use meaningless placeholders like RANDOM, DESIGN, ART, STUDIO, etc.

The composition should avoid mechanical centering and rigid PPT grids, prioritizing asymmetrical layouts, large areas of white space, misaligned color blocks, foreground-background occlusion, and contrasts in density. Create a viewing experience where the image reads as "simple and bold from afar, with texture, scene, and story up close."

The overall style should blend modern Eastern cultural posters, paper collage, watercolor materials, editorial design, and miniature narrative into a visual effect that feels sophisticated, natural, restrained, and culturally refined, while achieving the polish of a truly professional poster.

Avoid: Book cover vibes, oversized titles, traditional ink wash paintings, generic national style illustrations, realistic photographic backgrounds, PPT-style layouts, commercial ad vibes, element overload, excessive ornamentation, grimy paper, random noise, plastic sheen, 3D CGI, glass materials, neon colors, logos, watermarks, numbering, starburst decorations.

Create a charming vertical 4:5 mid-century travel picture-book illustration of [Destination], inspired by playful 1950s–60s European city books.
Depict the city as an affectionate, imperfect travel memory—not a map, postcard, architectural rendering, landmark collage, or cinematic panorama.
Include: 
• 1 distinctive primary landmark 
• 1 smaller secondary landmark 
• 1 distant/partially hidden local feature 
• 1 recognizable local vehicle
• 3–5 subtle everyday city details
• 5–6 ordinary people doing simple local activities
Compress these naturally into one imaginary street, plaza, park, or waterfront. Keep the primary landmark slightly off-center, with open foreground, shallow theatrical depth, gentle curves, and generous museum-white negative space. The city should be recognizable without feeling geographically accurate.
STYLE:
Hand-drawn picture-book illustration with loose charcoal/navy ink, trembling contours, crooked architecture, uneven proportions, sparse windows, simplified silhouettes, occasional double strokes, and minimal detail. Use the fewest lines necessary. Slightly awkward, intelligent, warm, humorous, and handmade.
PEOPLE:
Simple expressive figures with oversized heads, thin legs, narrow bodies, tiny faces, tilted accessories, and awkward but readable gestures. Show ordinary local life, not celebrities, models, stereotypes, or tourist clichés.
COLOR:
Use a restrained 6–7 color destination-specific palette with flat matte gouache shapes, uneven brush edges, white gaps, slight misregistration, and occasional color spilling beyond ink. Mostly unpainted sky/paper. No gradients or realistic shading.
MEMORY DISTORTION:
Gently compress geography and distort scale: distant landmarks may appear nearby, roads may curve strangely, buildings may overlap, and people/vehicles may be slightly oversized or undersized. Keep it balanced, affectionate, and culturally respectful.
OPTIONAL TEXT:
“[Destination]” in small uneven hand-drawn capitals near the bottom. No slogans, dates, labels, logos, or promotional text.
AVOID:
Photorealism, map-like accuracy, landmark checklists, aerial views, cinematic lighting, technical perspective, dense crowds, detailed ornament, polished vector art, CGI, 3D rendering, gradients, sepia/beige paper, artificial aging, distressed textures, and hyper-detailed watercolor.
Overall feeling: [Destination] remembered lovingly-recognizable, spacious, human, humorous, slightly improbable, and beautifully imperfect.
